about-us.rostushe_description: Rostushe is a village in Western Macedonia, located near the Radika River, which is known for its beauty and natural resources. The village is situated in a mountainous region, making it a pleasant place for nature lovers and hikers. Rostushe is known for its traditional architecture, hospitality, and still-preserved ancient customs and culture. Most of the village’s residents have moved to Western European countries (Italy, Germany, Switzerland, etc.), but during the summer and winter periods, they return to their homeland. Tourism is developing in this region thanks to its natural beauty and opportunities for active tourism, such as hiking and visiting historical and cultural sites. about-us.association_description: The sports association ‘Everesting Rostushe’ is an organization formed by citizens passionate about sports. It was established by a group of adult individuals who share a love for sports, with the goal of engaging in organized sports activities and competitions at all levels—municipal, national, and international. This association consists of adult members from the village of Rostushe and other sports enthusiasts who work towards achieving goals and objectives in the field of sports and physical activities. The headquarters of EVERSTING ROSTUSHE is located in the village of Rostushe, Municipality of Mavrovo and Rostushe.
about-us.association_intro: Mountaineering Club “Everesting Rostushe” is a mountain and sports club from the Mavrovo–Rostushe region, founded to promote mountain sports, a healthy active lifestyle, and the development of youth outdoor activities. The club actively organizes races, hiking tours, educational events, and nature conservation actions.

overview.title: Bagrem Trail 11К / 520 D+
overview.description: Beginners and runners who enjoy dynamic and vivid sections will love our shortest trail — Bagrem Trail 11К. Starting from Rostushe village, it follows the Radika River, passes through authentic rural landscapes to Janche (checkpoint), then loops back via Adzievci to the finish in Rostushe.

card1.title: Know the limits
card1.text: 27K starts at 08:00 with a 9-hour limit. 11K starts at 10:00 with a 4-hour limit.

card2.title: Carry the right gear
card2.text: Mandatory gear can be checked during the race, and missing gear can lead to penalties or disqualification.

card3.title: Be self-reliant
card3.text: The race is run in semi-autonomy, so runners must be ready to manage themselves in mountain conditions.

card4.title: Respect the mountain
card4.text: Stay on marked routes, do not litter, and respect nature, volunteers, and other runners.

facts.title: Race essentials
facts.subtitle: Quick facts from the official rules and regulations.
facts.rule1: Outside assistance is allowed only at refreshment stations.
facts.rule2: Pacers and third parties without a bib are not allowed to accompany runners on course.
facts.rule3: If a runner abandons outside an official checkpoint, they must inform the organizer immediately.
facts.rule4: The organizer may adapt routes or equipment rules if weather or safety conditions require it.

rules.title: Rules center
rules.subtitle: Read the official Macedonian rules directly on the page and use the summary cards on the right for a clearer runner-friendly overview.
rules.viewerText: This document is only available in Macedonian. For more details, feel free to contact us.
rules.summary1: The event takes place on 15 August 2026 and includes two races: 27K and 11K.
rules.summary2: Participation is at each runner’s own responsibility and requires physical and mental readiness.
rules.summary3: The race takes place in semi-autonomy, so runners must be prepared for changing mountain conditions and self-management.
rules.summary4: Runners must stay on the marked route and follow official instructions and checkpoint procedures.
rules.summary5: The organizer may change the route, stop the race, or update required gear for safety reasons.
rules.summary6: Respect for nature, volunteers, local community, and other runners is a core rule.

gear.title: Mandatory gear
gear.common2: Bib attached to the front of the body

penalties.title: Penalties & disqualification
penalties.item1: Leaving the marked route can lead to a time penalty or disqualification.
penalties.item2: Refusing a mandatory gear check can lead to disqualification.
penalties.item3: Not carrying mandatory gear can lead to disqualification or a time penalty.
penalties.item4: Littering, threatening volunteers, or unsportsmanlike behavior can lead to disqualification.
penalties.item5: Using another runner’s bib or racing with an invalid bib is not allowed.
